stages.name: Radar Archive Pipeline
stages.notes: Windows Task Scheduler auto-collecting PNGs every 5min since 2026-05-22. Audit 2026-07-10: 11,705 PNGs, radar.zarr has 11,610 frames current through 2026-07-10 00:05 UTC — 49/90 days (~54%). All 4 SG-Weather scheduled tasks ran today with LastResult 0. Coverage: 35 of 47 complete days >=240 frames; low days (travel/shutdown): Jun 21 (222), Jun 28 (182), Jun 30 (234), Jul 7 (228), Jul 9 (196). Mean frames/day: Jun 272.6, Jul 265.3. PNG->zarr ingest automated via '\SG-Weather\SG-Weather Radar Preprocess' daily 08:00 SGT. Target: 90 days = ~Aug 20, 2026. FIX 2026-07-10: zarr time axis had 13 monotonicity violations (batch appends backfilled older frames); archive re-sorted via preprocess_radar.py --repair and ensure_sorted_archive() now enforces global order after every append — required for RadarDataset positional windows (Stage 4) and frame lookups. Audit 2026-07-18: 13,556 frames current through 2026-07-17 23:20 UTC; 56 days with data (~62% of 90-day target, pace holds for ~Aug 20); 41/54 full days >=240 frames; new low days Jul 12 (172) + Jul 13 (174) (laptop off). Time axis verified strictly increasing (Jul 10 sort repair holding). ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED 2026-07-18 (supersedes same-day 'QC escalation' theory): the 862 all-NaN frames were NOT NEA outages — they were write-path corruption: interrupted/racing zarr appends (laptop shutdown mid-append; wake-time task race) commit timestamps to the time axis without writing rain_rate rows, zarr silently serves fill_value=NaN, and skip-by-timestamp never retries. Evidence: 66 NaN frames had full-size rainy PNGs, NaN runs align with 288-frame chunk boundaries and shutdown windows, all 862 PNGs existed on disk. ALL 862 HEALED 2026-07-18 via new heal_blank_frames() in preprocess_radar.py (re-converts PNGs, writes rows in place); runs after every preprocess so future interrupted appends self-heal; --heal flag for standalone. Archive verified 0 NaN frames. COLLECTION HARDENING 2026-07-18 (user constraint: laptop off up to 1 day max): NEA retention probed at >=120h (~6-7 days; Jul 12 still served at 145h, Jul 8 404 at ~10 days). 'SG-Weather Radar Scraper' rewired: --hours 25 -> 120, preprocess chained as action 2 (kills wake race where preprocess globbed PNGs mid-backfill), ExecutionTimeLimit PT2H; standalone 'SG-Weather Radar Preprocess' task DELETED (superseded by chain). scrape_radar.py now validates PNG magic bytes instead of '>280 bytes' (275b no-rain frames were being silently rejected). One-time 168h backfill run 2026-07-18 to recover Jul 12-13 frames lost to the old 25h window. Laptop-off recovery now guaranteed for any window <=~5 days. RE-INGEST 2026-08-11 (tasks 3.7 + 3.8): the archive was rebuilt from all 21,005 PNGs onto the corrected native 120x217 grid — every frame before this date was the bottom-right corner of the NEA image, upsampled, with a non-monotonic colour scale. Migration ran expand->migrate->contract per Pattern L: built radar_v2.zarr alongside, passed 9/9 pre-declared validation checks, renamed into place with writers paused; radar.zarr.old retained pending a soak-period contract gate. Derived artifacts rebuilt (radar_stats.json now n=21005 vs the stale n=2357 from Jun 5; geocode cache re-indexed in place preserving all hand-curated entries; flood_eval_dataset.parquet rebuilt). Post-migration verification: 0 NaN, strictly increasing, PNG/zarr counts in exact sync, preprocess idempotent (21,005 skipped/0 errors), scheduled scrape->preprocess chain appended 5 frames with LastTaskResult 0, and a 100-step training smoke test passed on the new grid (loss 0.4313, stage flag correctly withheld). Day count unaffected: still 81/90, ETA 2026-08-20.

tasks.description: Self-healing ingest: heal_blank_frames() recovers NaN rows from PNGs on every preprocess run
Georeference correction: replace the 480x480-derived crop with the true NEA bounds and ingest the native 217x120 domain
tasks.notes: WORSE THAN TRACKED: the crop was not merely miscalibrated. On a 120x217 image the guard clamped rows 80:270 -> 80:120 and cols 130:350 -> 130:217, keeping the BOTTOM-RIGHT CORNER (rows 67-100%, cols 60-100%) and bilinear-upsampling 40x87 -> 190x220; the lat/lon coords (1.0-1.6N, 103.5-104.1E) were fiction. Fixed: full native domain, no crop, no resample. Bounds lat 1.1450-1.4572, lon 103.565-104.130 from weather.gov.sg page source, corroborated by cheeaun/checkweather-sg; cross-check 0.002602 deg/px lat vs 0.002604 lon = square pixels ~0.29 km, matching the NEA product spec. PHYSICAL VALIDATION (the acceptance gate, per L009): rain within ~1.5 km of geocoded flood cells at event time went from 19% of events (median peak 0.00 mm/hr) to 100% (median peak 51.57 mm/hr). This also resolves the residual half of L008 — flood cells read 0 mm/hr because of this crop, not because FLOOD_RISK warnings precede rain.

tasks.description: Alpha-aware colour conversion + exact-match 33-colour NEA LUT (replaces nearest-RGB against 11 anchors)
tasks.notes: ORIGINAL PREMISE DISPROVED: alpha is binary (0/255) archive-wide and transparent RGB is always (0,0,0), which already mapped to 0 mm/hr — dropping alpha was harmless, and these PNGs carry no basemap (they are pure overlays). The real source of the 'phantom drizzle <=~4 mm/hr floor' was BILINEAR RESAMPLING of a banded field: upsampling turned 9 discrete values into 7,302 and pushed nonzero cells from 68.5% to 95.8% on a rainy frame. Removed with the resize. THIRD DEFECT FOUND: nearest-RGB matching against 11 anchors while NEA uses exactly 33 discrete colours produced 8/33 NON-MONOTONIC mappings (lightest teal -> 2.0 mm/hr while 5 brighter cyans -> 1.0; magenta 255,0,255 -> 80 while a lighter magenta -> 100). Replaced with an exact-match LUT over all 33 colours; unknown colours are counted and reported, never snapped. Ramp ordering derived from the archive by three agreeing methods (distance-transform depth, spatial-adjacency graph walk, RGB continuity); absolute values log-uniform 0.5-100 mm/hr = 0.719 dBR/band, justified by the product being dBR. 0 opaque pixels archive-wide fall outside the ramp. Alpha now masked explicitly regardless.

tasks.description: NaN-aware sample filtering in RadarDataset (exclude windows containing blank all-NaN frames)
tasks.notes: 862 blank frames archive-wide sit at valid timestamps, so they passed the 4.7 contiguity filter; 896 NaN-poisoned samples reached the splits (train 659, val 130, test 107). Fix: frame-validity mask (any-NaN = blank; archive is perfectly bimodal, 0 partial-NaN frames) + cumsum window check over the full sample span, symmetric with the gap filter; compute_stats made nan-safe (nanmean/nanstd/nanmax). Existing radar_stats.json (Jun 5, pre-blanks) deliberately left untouched to keep normalisation constants stable. Post-fix repro (tasks/repro/nan_samples_repro.py): 0 NaN samples in all splits; drops train 667/val 130/test 109.

stages.name: Evaluation & Flash Flood Map
stages.notes: Ground-truth pipeline live: collect_flood_labels.py (Telegram, daily 09:00 SGT scheduled task, conda env) -> flood_labels.parquet; build_flood_eval_dataset.py cross-references labels to radar.zarr -> flood_eval_dataset.parquet. CRITICAL FIX 2026-07-10: '[HH:MM hours]' tags in PUB messages are SGT wall-clock but were stored as UTC — every label was 8h late and all geocoded flood cells read 0.0 mm/hr (see lessons L009; supersedes the L007/L008 'verified' claim). Collector now parses SGT -> UTC (nearest-day resolution); parquet rebuilt from raw messages.json. Rebuilt eval dataset 2026-07-10: 34 labels through 2026-07-08 (23 RAIN_WARNING, 11 FLOOD_RISK, 0 FLASH_FLOOD), 31/34 radar-matched (11/11 flood events), rain now visible at geocoded cells (e.g. Jalan Boon Lay 4.7 mm/hr near-cell at warning minute). Geocode cache: all 10 strings resolved — KPE slip-road hand-fixed 2026-07-10 to the Buangkok East Drive junction (1.3775, 103.9090, cell 70,149); all 11 flood events now carry spatial cells. FULLY AUTOMATED 2026-07-10: 'SG-Weather Telegram Labels' task (daily 09:00 SGT, conda env) now chains collect -> geocode (cache/gazetteer first, OneMap failures degrade to unresolved without breaking the chain) -> build_flood_eval_dataset; ExecutionTimeLimit raised PT10M -> PT20M; chain verified end-to-end (exit 0, parquets refreshed). evaluation_report.json (2026-06-18) is a smoke-run placeholder — not a real result. NOT yet wired into evaluate.py (would change Stage 5 semantics; awaiting approval). Audit 2026-07-18: label chain healthy end-to-end (daily runs exit 0, state.json last_run current); still 34 labels, none since Jul 8 — verified against the live PUB channel web preview that the channel itself has been quiet (newest post matches our last stored message), collector not at fault. Notable: radar showed large heavy-rain footprints Jul 10/12/16 with no PUB heavy-rain advisory — channel may only post a subset of NEA warnings.
